description: Table 1 is a photograph-free, text-only data table (image modality: rendered table, no axes, no scale bar, no schematic) that reports tensile properties of Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel specimens annealed at various temperatures. The table has five columns with headers printed exactly as: "Annealing temperature (°C)", "Ultimate strength (MPa)", "Yield strength (MPa)", "Ultimate elongation (%)", and "Product of strength and ductility (GPa%)". Eight data rows are listed for annealing temperatures 700, 800, 850, 900, 950, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C, with row values as follows: 700 °C—971 MPa, 837 MPa, 4.8%, 5 GPa%; 800 °C—877 MPa, 702 MPa, 7.8%, 7 GPa%; 850 °C—879 MPa, 693 MPa, 21.7%, 19 GPa%; 900 °C—855 MPa, 651 MPa, 36.6%, 31 GPa%; 950 °C—804 MPa, 581 MPa, 26.6%, 21 GPa%; 1000 °C—763 MPa, 557 MPa, 16.2%, 12 GPa%; 1100 °C—671 MPa, 518 MPa, 12%, 8 GPa%; 1200 °C—611 MPa, 495 MPa, 4.8%, 3 GPa%. The table therefore shows that ultimate strength and yield strength fall monotonically as annealing temperature rises, whereas ultimate elongation and the product of strength and ductility both peak at 900 °C (36.6% and 31 GPa%) and drop sharply on either side. No graphical panels, micrographs or spectra are present; the whole group is this single table.

subfigures.description: Single tabular panel, five columns (Annealing temperature (°C), Ultimate strength (MPa), Yield strength (MPa), Ultimate elongation (%), Product of strength and ductility (GPa%)) and eight data rows covering annealing temperatures 700 to 1200 °C, with the highest elongation (36.6%) and highest strength–ductility product (31 GPa%) at 900 °C and the highest strengths (971/837 MPa) at 700 °C.

observations.observation: The table lists exactly eight annealing temperatures: 700, 800, 850, 900, 950, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C.
At 900 °C the table gives ultimate strength 855 MPa, yield strength 651 MPa, ultimate elongation 36.6% and product of strength and ductility 31 GPa%.
The maximum ultimate strength in the table is 971 MPa with 837 MPa yield strength at 700 °C; the minimum is 611 MPa ultimate with 495 MPa yield at 1200 °C.
Ultimate elongation is lowest at both ends of the range, 4.8% at 700 °C and 4.8% at 1200 °C, and highest at 900 °C (36.6%).
The product of strength and ductility follows the elongation trend, peaking at 31 GPa% at 900 °C and falling to 3 GPa% at 1200 °C and 5 GPa% at 700 °C.
Both ultimate strength and yield strength decrease monotonically with increasing annealing temperature from 700 °C to 1200 °C.
The caption states the specimens were annealed at various temperatures and that the product of strength and ductility equals ultimate strength multiplied by ultimate elongation.
The citing text states the product of strength and ductility reaches its best value when the annealing temperature is 900 °C.

The citing text states that after annealing at 900 °C for 1 h the ultimate strength, yield strength, ultimate elongation and product of strength and ductility are 855 MPa, 651 MPa, 36.6% and 31 GPa%, respectively, matching the table row.
The citing text states the ultimate elongation first increases from 700 °C to 900 °C and then decreases from 900 °C to 1200 °C, with the most violent change in the 800–1000 °C range.
The citing text states that the change in the product of strength and ductility is mainly decided by the change in ultimate elongation.

The paper abstract (citing context) states that the phases in the annealed specimens mainly included ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide, and that the dissolution temperature for κ-carbide lies between 850 °C and 900 °C, which brackets the 900 °C peak in the table.
